front: What is EventEmitter in one sentence?
back: One-line: pub/sub inside a Node process — decouple producers from listeners; foundation of streams, HTTP, and most core APIs.

front: Explain the mental model of EventEmitter (how the system thinks).
back: EventEmitter is Node's observer pattern: objects emit named events; registered listeners run synchronously in registration order (unless setImmediate/async inside handler).

front: Explain the mental model of Node.js run as a non-privileged user (how the system thinks).

front: What is spawn in one sentence?
back: One-line: run an external binary with piped stdio — no shell by default; use for ffmpeg, git, openssl, and other CLI tools from Node.

front: Explain the mental model of spawn (how the system thinks).
back: child_process.spawn(command, args[], options) starts a child process and returns a ChildProcess with .stdin, .stdout, .stderr streams. Unlike exec, no shell is invoked unless shell: true — safer and faster for fixed binaries.

front: Symptom: Hangs forever — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Child waits for stdin · Fix: stdio: 'ignore' or close stdin

front: Symptom: Buffer fills; process stalls — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: stdout not consumed · Fix: Pipe and drain stdout/stderr

front: Symptom: Shell injection — what do you check and fix?

front: Gotcha with spawn: what silently fails?
back: Unread pipes deadlock — if stdout buffer fills (~64KB default), child blocks. Always consume or 'ignore'.

front: When should you NOT use spawn?
back: Run another Node script with IPC — use fork for built-in message channel. Tiny one-liner, small output — execFile is simpler. CPU work in-process — use worker threads, not shelling out.

front: What is Node.js Worker Threads in one sentence?
back: One-line: true OS threads inside one Node process for CPU-heavy work — share memory optionally via SharedArrayBuffer; don't replace cluster for HTTP scaling.

front: Explain the mental model of Node.js Worker Threads (how the system thinks).
back: Worker threads run JavaScript (or wasm) in parallel with the main thread's event loop. Message passing is default; shared memory is opt-in.

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for Node.js Worker Threads?
back: Main thread (event loop) ←postMessage→ Worker thread(s)

front: Given a broken Node.js Worker Threads setup, what is your first validation command?
back: Main thread (event loop) ←postMessage→ Worker thread(s)

front: What are the production-safe defaults for Node.js Worker Threads?
back: Requires --experimental-worker flags only on very old Node; modern Node is stable. HTTP headers may need Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy if serving SAB to browsers — N/A for pure backend.

front: Symptom: Worker exits immediately — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Uncaught exception in worker · Fix: worker.on('error'); wrap worker bootstrap in try/catch

front: Symptom: Main thread still blocks — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Heavy work still on main · Fix: Move computation into worker file entirely

front: Symptom: Memory doubles — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Large messages copied · Fix: Transfer ArrayBuffers; use SharedArrayBuffer

front: Symptom: ERR_WORKER_OUT_OF_MEMORY — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Worker heap limit · Fix: Split work; increase --max-old-space-size sparingly

front: Symptom: Slower than expected — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Worker startup cost · Fix: Pool workers; amortize over batch

front: Symptom: Can't access DOM/db conn — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: By design · Fix: Pass serializable data; use connection pool on main

front: Gotcha with Node.js Worker Threads: what silently fails?
back: postMessage clones most objects — expensive for MB payloads. Use transferable ArrayBuffer list.

front: When should you NOT use Node.js Worker Threads?
back: HTTP request scaling — use clustering or horizontal pods. I/O-bound work — event loop + async I/O is simpler and faster. Untrusted user code — use separate process/container sandbox, not worker alone.
